method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across power that gives life through suffering accepted for others, the fruits of education in character and fellowship, miracles, evidence and recognition, the station of the divine Educator, a word that renews creation, the promise and the voice, capacity, veils and the act of seeing, sovereignty and its purpose, the call from within captivity, encounters and recollections, an influence that continues, and receiving power through service. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. Imported wording checked separately; version differences remain explicit. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: yet His spirit is in joy and delight through the love of God. Nothing can sadden Him
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s brief statement that His spirit is in joy through the love of God and nothing can sadden Him; carries the opening contrast between outward affliction and inward joy.

selected.text: Today, through the blessing of the Most Holy Name, the world appeareth as paradise itself.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that through the blessing of the Most Holy Name the world appeareth as paradise; a brief image of a world made new.

selected.text: through a single letter from Him was everything created with the ornament of luminous glory
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that through a single letter from Him everything was created with luminous glory; complements the authorized passage on the creative letter.

selected.text: necks were laid low before Him, and all heads bowed down to Him; all faces turned humbly towards Him, and all voices were hushed
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: the Most Glorious Kingdom, raise the divine standard in Tokyo and cry out: O people! The Sun of Reality has risen and illumined the horizons
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s call to raise the divine standard in Tokyo and proclaim the risen Sun of Reality; a distinctive practical summons.

selected.text: Verses like rain, nay greater, are continually streaming down and descending, encompassing the world.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of verses streaming down like rain, nay greater, encompassing the world; a vivid statement of abundant utterance.

selected.text: Now, praise be to God, the trees of this Revelation are adorned with the fruits of love and knowledge.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the trees of this Revelation are adorned with the fruits of love and knowledge; names the fruits of education in one line.

selected.text: With what power You have made the proud ones the captives of love and have united the East with the West!
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá exclaiming at the power that made the proud the captives of love and united East and West; a compact statement of transformed relationships.

selected.text: He possesseth a Name which, were He to cast it upon poison, would transform it into the Most Great Antidote
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on a Name that, cast upon poison, would turn it into the Most Great Antidote; the catalogue rendering of this image of transforming power.

selected.text: All things are captive in the grasp of His power and all the wealthy are poor at the threshold of His riches.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that all things are captive in His grasp and the wealthy poor at His threshold; a compact image of power and need.

selected.text: God Who manifested Himself and uttered a Word whereby all who are in the heavens and earth were thunderstruck
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on God manifesting Himself and uttering a Word whereby all in heaven and earth were thunderstruck; a brief statement of the impact of the Word.

selected.text: The penetration of His Word and the potency of influence must be so great as to humble even his worst enemies.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the penetration of a Manifestation’s Word must be great enough to humble His worst enemies; opens the section on evidence with a test of influence.

selected.text: By God! This is He at Whose walking the Kingdom of God walketh behind Him, and the Spirit proclaimeth before Him
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of the Kingdom of God walking behind Him and the Spirit proclaiming before Him; a brief image of accompanying power.

selected.text: The Book has been revealed, verses are witnessed, and divine commandments and laws are present before all faces.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the Book is revealed, verses witnessed and laws present before all faces; names the revealed Book itself as the evidence.

selected.text: We have built for thee from the iron rods of utterance that which will not be altered by the vicissitudes of time
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of a structure built from the iron rods of utterance that time cannot alter; a memorable image of enduring words.

selected.text: Glorified be He Who speaketh the truth and summoneth all unto His Self, the One Who hath dominion over the worlds.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh glorifying Him Who speaks the truth and summons all unto His Self; a brief statement of the call addressed to the world.

selected.text: Because of your spiritual receptivity God hath sent me to Stuttgart in order to proclaim the Kingdom of Baha'u'llah.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that God sent him to Stuttgart because of the friends’ spiritual receptivity; links receptivity with service.

selected.text: through His complete power and conquering might, hath transformed the prison of 'Akka into the Most Exalted Paradise
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on power that transformed the prison of ‘Akka into the Most Exalted Paradise; a memorable image of captivity transformed.

selected.text: Powerful art Thou to do Thy pleasure. No God is there but Thee, the All-Glorious, Whose help is implored by all men
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Baha'u'llah teaches him so well that after a few months Azziz will become well-known for his extraordinary intelligence.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that Bahá’u’lláh would teach Azziz so well that he would become known for extraordinary intelligence; a distinctive example of learning conferred.

selected.text: The Promise hath come to pass, and the Promised One calleth aloud before all faces, yet most of the people perceive not.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the Promised One calls aloud before all faces, yet most perceive not; a necessary note that declaration is not reception.

selected.text: The fragrances of Thy love have thereby been wafted over Thy cities and have encompassed all the dwellers of Thy realm
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: The more they increased in opposition, the more We increased in manifestation, to spite them. Thus was the matter decreed
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the more they increased in opposition the more He increased in manifestation; a memorable statement of power growing through resistance.

selected.text: It was from this sure and certain knowledge He spoke, when He said: 'All power is given unto Me, in Heaven and in earth'.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: They are indeed God's proof amidst His creation, His evidence unto His creatures, and His testimony unto all in His kingdom.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the Manifestations as God’s proof amidst His creation and His testimony unto all; a compact definition of their evidential role.

selected.text: Neither prison can withhold Him from God, nor can the hosts of earth frighten Him. He is, verily, the Strong, the Trustworthy.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that neither prison can withhold Him from God nor hosts frighten Him; joins captivity with inward freedom.

selected.text: By the "Cloud of Mercy," the heat and the light of the Sun, and by the life-giving breeze this divine gardener is strengthened.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on the divine gardener strengthened by the Cloud of Mercy, the Sun’s heat and light and the life-giving breeze; carries the introduction’s garden image.

selected.text: while He was a prisoner in the Most Great Prison, He raised up this mighty Cause and created a great commotion in East and West
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s statement that as a prisoner Bahá’u’lláh raised up the Cause and stirred East and West; a brief summary of the call from captivity.

selected.text: Were He to move, with Him would move the hosts of the unseen, then the Concourse on High, then the realities of all worlds.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that were He to move, the hosts of the unseen and the realities of all worlds would move with Him; an image of the world moving with the Manifestation.

selected.text: We have, with the hands of power, unsealed the choice sealed wine of immortality - drink thou of it in My Name, the All-Powerful.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s invitation to drink the sealed wine of immortality unsealed by the hands of power; a direct invitation to receive.

selected.text: This is a Day wherein the Word hath appeared in the form of a human being and calleth all unto the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the Word has appeared in the form of a human being calling all to God; the guide’s plainest link between the Word and a human life.

selected.text: Although to all outward appearance the Blessed Perfection was an exile, yet he moved with such power and manifested such majesty!
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that though outwardly an exile Bahá’u’lláh moved with power and majesty; a brief recollection of outward weakness and inward majesty.

selected.text: otherwise, by Him Who causeth My tongue to speak His praise, We could have subdued all who are on earth with but one word from Him
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that He could have subdued all on earth with one word; a necessary note on forbearance as chosen restraint.

selected.text: I walk at all times before all who dwell in the realm of possibility. I see and I hear, and I am the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that He walks before all in the realm of possibility, seeing and hearing; a first-person declaration of encompassing awareness.

selected.text: My hair is My Messenger. It is calling aloud at all times upon the branch of Fire within the hallowed and luminous garden of Paradise
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s Tablet of the Hair declaring His hair His Messenger calling upon the branch of Fire; a distinctive image of every part of His being as a voice.

selected.text: Blessed is the soul that hath attained unto the Word of God - verily it is among the most exalted of creation in the Preserved Tablet.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh blessing the soul that has attained unto the Word of God; links recognition with human exaltation.

selected.text: All things are established through My Will, as they were established before, and none comprehend this save those possessed of insight.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that all things are established through His Will, comprehended only by those with insight; joins power with the need for insight.

selected.text: This is a Day the like of which the eye of creation hath not seen. Abandon what ye possess and turn unto God, the Lord of all worlds.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to abandon what one possesses on a Day the eye of creation has not seen; closes the section with an invitation.

selected.text: By God! The All-Merciful hath come with such a proof as all who are in the heavens and on earth cannot withstand, did ye but know.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s oath that the All-Merciful has come with a proof none in heaven or earth can withstand; a brief declaration of the force of His proof.

selected.text: Tribulation shall not deter Us from that which We have purposed, nor shall destiny prevent Us from that which We have been bidden.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that neither tribulation nor destiny shall deter Him from His purpose; a concise statement of steadfastness.

selected.text: Rejoice thou that the Most Great Ocean hath turned towards thee from this remote station and calleth thee unto God, purely for His sake.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to rejoice that the Most Great Ocean calls the addressee unto God purely for His sake; closes the linked passages with an invitation for God alone.

selected.text: Consider the loftiness of this Cause, its exaltation, its glory and its station, and then observe the baseness of these ignorant people.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to consider the loftiness of the Cause and then the baseness of its ignorant opponents; a brief contrast of station and reception.

selected.text: So in such a state how can you resist Baha'u'llah Who fears neither kings nor governments, but rather stands against the whole world
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking how one can resist Bahá’u’lláh Who feared neither kings nor governments; a brief conclusion from the encounters.

selected.text: when the appointed hour arrived He appeared through the power of Truth, and toward Him have turned the sincere ones from every direction
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on His appearance at the appointed hour through the power of Truth, with the sincere turning to Him; links timing with response.

selected.text: By God! Through a movement of His finger all things were drawn unto Him. Thus was the decree ordained, if ye be of them that understand.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that through a movement of His finger all things were drawn unto Him; a compact image of attracting power.

selected.text: Verily thy Lord is not prevented by anything from anything … Such is God's way among His servants and His sovereignty over His creation
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that God is not prevented by anything from anything; opens the section on freedom and authority.

selected.text: Do people think that the Remembrance seeth not their deeds? Nay, for He is the Witness from God, their Lord, over all the worlds together.
selected.reason: The Báb’s statement that the Remembrance sees people’s deeds as the Witness from God over all the worlds; a brief statement of the Manifestation as witness.

selected.text: We have sent down the Command and expounded the verses that perchance men may ponder upon God's sovereignty and His firm and mighty Cause.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on verses expounded that men may ponder upon God’s sovereignty; gives the purpose of the verses as reflection.

selected.text: Although the divine hand of change and transformation is encompassing and engaged, yet verily We have veiled the people with a mighty veil.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the hand of transformation is at work, yet He has veiled the people with a mighty veil; a necessary qualification on visible change.

selected.text: The Breath of God awakened Him and commanded Him to raise His voice. When He awoke, He arose and called all to God, the Lord of the worlds.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: That Light of Truth - its outpouring is all-encompassing and its grace is perfect, whether in the Day of Manifestation or after its setting.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s statement that the outpouring of the Light of Truth is perfect in the Day of Manifestation and after its setting; a concise statement of continuing grace.

selected.text: And 'Ali came with the truth, and with Him were clear signs, a single letter of which would suffice all who are in the heavens and the earth.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that ‘Ali came with the truth and with clear signs, a single letter of which would suffice all in heaven and earth; the sufficiency of a single sign.

selected.text: The hands of divine bounty have nurtured all mankind, and, through the tongue of the Manifestations of His own Self, have announced unto all who dwell in the worlds the glad-tidings of the appearance of the Most Great Name
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on the hands of divine bounty nurturing mankind and announcing through the Manifestations the appearance of the Most Great Name; opens the promise with nurture and glad tidings.

selected.text: As for my power, it is an outpouring from the outpourings of Baha'u'llah. He is my supporter. He is my light of guidance. He is my fire of love
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s statement that his own power is an outpouring of Bahá’u’lláh’s, his supporter and light; identifies the source of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s strength.

selected.text: He is, in truth, the Dawning-Place of divine revelation, the Dayspring of inspiration, the Quickener of bones, and with Him lieth the final word
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh naming the Dawning-Place of revelation the Quickener of bones with Whom lies the final word; a compact image of life-giving authority.

selected.text: Ask whatsoever ye please. Powerful is He to do what He willeth. Nothing whatsoever, be it of the past or of the future, can frustrate His Will
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: What can earthly power do against celestial might? And what can contingent darkness accomplish against divine light? This has been tried before
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking what earthly power can do against celestial might; a concise argument from history.

selected.text: But ponder and consider how, though He be Lord of the Invisible Realm, the rays of His benediction still shine unceasingly upon this nether world.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on the rays of the Lord of the Invisible Realm still shining upon this world; the light whose setting does not end its gifts.

selected.text: That which had never appeared in the world hath appeared, and the divine fragrance hath wafted, and the breeze hath blown, and the Ark hath sailed
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that what never appeared has appeared, the breeze has blown and the Ark has sailed; a brief image of a new Day.

selected.text: He hath arisen to promote the Cause of God in such wise that none on earth can turn Him back, nor can the might of any froward oppressor disturb Him
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on arising to promote the Cause so that none can turn Him back; a concise statement of resolve.

selected.text: This is not possible through human power. This is possible through the dominion of the Kingdom. It is possible through the Breath of the Holy Spirit.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that such change is not possible through human power but through the dominion of the Kingdom and the breath of the Holy Spirit; names the source of transformation.

selected.text: He Who speaketh is verily the Dawning-Place of revelation and the Rising-Point of inspiration. To this beareth witness My tongue and My wondrous pen.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that He Who speaks is the Dawning-Place of revelation, attested by His tongue and pen; a brief declaration of the speaker’s station.

selected.text: Despite the tribulations that surround Me, My Most Exalted Pen hath not ceased, and moveth at all times in celebration of God, the Lord of all names.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that despite tribulations His Pen has not ceased to celebrate God; a first-person witness of remembrance in affliction.

selected.text: But with one burning effulgence from the Dawning-Place of the unseen Kingdom, He so dissolved and scattered those dense clouds that minds were amazed
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on one burning effulgence dissolving the dense clouds so that minds were amazed; an image of light overcoming obstruction.

selected.text: The verses have encompassed all directions and the Day-Star of proof hath shone forth from the horizon of the Pen of the will of your Lord, the All-Merciful.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of the verses encompassing all directions and the Day-Star of proof shining from the Pen; joins utterance with the image of the sun.

selected.text: Your belief will never increase Us nor will your rejection decrease Us, and all who are in the heavens and earth today are but as a handful of aged clay
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that belief neither increases nor rejection decreases Him, all being as a handful of clay; a qualification on His independence of response.

selected.text: the signs of bounty are made manifest: He turneth the mote into a sun, and, through the radiance of the effulgent splendours of the Most Great Name, He maketh the drop to become an ocean
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of bounty that turns the mote into a sun and the drop into an ocean; a memorable statement of capacities brought to life.

selected.text: The Mount speaks and says: "Blessed am I in that I have attained unto Him Who conversed with Him Who guided Moses to the path of God, the Lord of all creation."
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh giving voice to the Mount, which blesses its attainment unto the One Who guided Moses; a memorable image of creation recognizing the promise.

selected.text: Through Him the valley of Mecca overflowed and the mouth of the Hijaz smiled, and through Him was raised the standard of Truth and lowered the banner of metaphor
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the One through Whom Mecca overflowed and the standard of truth replaced the banner of metaphor; links fulfilment to Muhammad’s revelation.

selected.text: Now the people of truth cry out that the divine light has illumined the horizons and the divine call has reached the ears of East and West from the Tree of Truth.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s statement that the divine call has reached East and West from the Tree of Truth; a brief image of spreading influence.

selected.text: Though ye see Him vanquished, by My life He is the Victor over all who are in the heavens and earth. And though ye see Him subjugated, He is in truth the Subduer.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that though seen vanquished He is the Victor, though subjugated the Subduer; carries the paradox of outward weakness and true power.

selected.text: Among the miracles which distinguish this sacred Dispensation is this, that women have evinced a greater boldness than men when enlisted in the ranks of the Faith.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: He Who conversed on Sinai hath seated Himself upon the throne of Revelation in a spot which God hath made the Dayspring of Light and the Dawning-place of His signs
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that He Who conversed on Sinai is seated upon the throne of Revelation; links the voice of Sinai with the present Revelation.

selected.text: in chains, and at times led captive from land to land. Yet in all conditions the shrill voice of the Pen was heard and the Call was raised. The heedlessness of the world did not prevent the Ancient Beauty from His purpose
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on being led captive from land to land while the voice of the Pen was still heard; a narrative of exile and proclamation.

selected.text: The Promised One hath come with a sovereignty that hath conquered the realms of meaning and utterance, and with a power before which no power in the world can stand.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on the Promised One’s sovereignty conquering the realms of meaning and utterance; names the realm in which His power works.

selected.text: I am a lamp of the love of God and a star of truth and reconciliation … souls will be educated and arise to fulfill the divine teachings and spread the Spirit of God
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing himself as a lamp of the love of God through whose service souls will be educated; his own account of service.

selected.text: The light of Christ was like unto the light of the Sun. He was the center, the reservoir, the power-house of illumination, but others received their light from him.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on the light of Christ as the centre, reservoir and power-house of illumination from which others received light; a clear image of source and reflection.

selected.text: The Day of Resurrection hath come, and in it the Self-Subsisting One of Names hath arisen with a sovereignty that encompasseth all who are in the heavens and on earth
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s announcement that the Day of Resurrection has come with a sovereignty encompassing all; a concise fulfilment declaration.

selected.text: Verily He strengtheneth whom He willeth and aideth whom He pleaseth and loveth him who loveth Him and remembereth in His kingdom him who remembereth Him on His earth
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on God strengthening whom He wills and remembering in His kingdom whoever remembers Him on earth; the reciprocity of remembrance.

selected.text: When the gate of heaven was opened and the Lord of Names appeared, agitation seized all in the realms of creation save those whom the hand of grace had taken hold of.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on the agitation that seized creation when the Lord of Names appeared, save those held by grace; links appearance with the trial of recognition.

selected.text: This is the Day whereon the Rock crieth out with the loudest voice: "Hasten with your hearts to the direction of the Beloved, O ye who are endued with understanding!"
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on the Rock crying to hasten with hearts toward the Beloved; a brief summons of the heart.

selected.text: On this Day there is no refuge for any soul, no haven for anyone, save beneath My shadow. Thus hath the command been sent down from the heaven of a glorious Name.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that there is no refuge on this Day save beneath His shadow; a concise statement of refuge.

selected.text: What greater honor can be imagined than the honor conferred by the Tongue of the Ancient of Days when He calleth to remembrance His loved ones in His Most Great Prison?
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: By God! The breezes of the All-Merciful have wafted from the direction of the All-Glorious, and by them are attracted the hearts of all who have believed and fear God.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s oath that the breezes of the All-Merciful attract the hearts of believers; keeps one image of the breeze of influence.

selected.text: Come forth that thou mayest hear and see that He hath appeared with a sovereignty before which every discerning mystic and every informed scholar hath bowed down.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s invitation to come forth and see a sovereignty before which mystics and scholars have bowed; joins sovereignty with personal witness.

selected.text: This is the reality of the situation - no seeker has the right to test. The Sought must test the seeker. The teacher must test the student, not the student the teacher.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s statement that no seeker has the right to test, for the Sought must test the seeker; a necessary qualification on demands for miraculous proof.

selected.text: If the world did not have capacity, there would not have been a Revelation. The very fact of Revelation is proof of capacity, from which magnificent results will appear
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the very fact of Revelation is proof of the world’s capacity; a foundational link between divine power and human capacity.

selected.text: Should the light of this station, even less than an atom thereof, be shed upon the world, all would exclaim: "This is from God's bounty, the Most High, the Most Great!"
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that less than an atom of this station’s light would make all exclaim at God’s bounty; complements the withheld splendour.

selected.text: His tongue speaketh in remembrance of God, His feet move toward the Intended One, His Pen moveth to mention Him, and with His finger He moveth the thread of existence
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing His tongue, feet and Pen moving in remembrance, and His finger moving the thread of existence; joins devotion with creative power.

selected.text: He hath come with truth and stood before the faces of the world, speaking as He willeth, such that no thing among all things, nor the might of princes, could prevent Him.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on the One Who stood before the world speaking as He willed, unhindered by princes; keeps one concise statement of unhindered speech.

selected.text: by His divine power, rent asunder the dense veils of contingent beings and, despite the opposition of the flies, established Himself unveiled and unhindered upon the throne
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on the One Who rent the veils of contingent beings and, despite the flies, established Himself unveiled; a memorable image of power amid opposition.

selected.text: The verses have been sent down and the evidences have appeared, and the sealed wine has been unsealed by the finger of God, the Omnipotent, the Supreme, the Self-Subsisting.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the verses have been sent down and the sealed wine unsealed by the finger of God; a memorable image of revelation as evidence.

selected.text: Look not upon creatures and their works, but rather upon the Truth and His sovereignty. Thus hath the matter been decreed from before God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to look not upon creatures and their works but upon the Truth and His sovereignty; turns the reader from appearances to the source.

selected.text: He that directed himself hither, and attained unto the presence of his Lord, made mention of you before the throne, whence We have made mention of you as a bounty on Our part
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on mentioning the friends before the throne as a bounty; a concrete instance of remembrance received.

selected.text: the like of which no man hath ever before sustained.  My Lord, the All-Knowing, testifieth to the truth of My words.  I have summoned the people unto none save God, thy Lord and the Lord of the worlds, and have endured for love of Him such afflictions as the eye of creation

selected.text: from His grace - outwardly thou art far but inwardly near. He is the Kind Bestower. The whole world was brought from nothingness into being for this blessed Day, yet heedlessness and pride have prevented all from hearkening to the call of the Speaker on Sinai
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the whole world was created for this Day, yet heedlessness keeps people from hearing; joins encouragement with a warning.

selected.text: Do ye dispute with Him Who hath come from the Dayspring of the Cause with power and sovereignty? He hath indeed beheld such signs of His Lord as cannot be described in words.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asking whether people dispute with Him Who has beheld signs beyond words; ends the declarations with a challenge to response.

He doeth what He willeth and ordaineth what He pleaseth. He is the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on appearing at the appointed time, unhindered by men or the oppression of deniers; joins timing, knowledge and steadfastness.

selected.text: God hath made the likeness of His Command as the likeness of the sun which God causeth to rise times beyond any one's reckoning save His own, whereupon all are illumined by a single sun; and He causeth it to set times beyond any one's reckoning save His own, whereupon all await it. Say: I am the first whom God created from a beginning that hath no beginning, and made me the Sun of His Manifestation unto all the worlds.
selected.reason: The Báb likening God’s Command to a sun rising and setting times beyond reckoning, and naming Himself the Sun of His Manifestation; a foundational image of successive revelation.

selected.text: life of Him Whom God shall make manifest, that Manifestation is more wondrous than the Manifestation of Muhammad before, but people do not understand nor remember. What God revealed to Muhammad over twenty-three years, if God had wished, He could have revealed to him in two days and two nights. Say: If you desire, We shall surely reveal to you, for We are powerful over that. If it is not detailed in two days and two nights and written before Us by one who tires not, this is from God's command, the Mighty, the Inaccessible. Is there any proof equal to this, if you would but remember? God manifested Muhammad among the Arabs, while I was raised among those who cannot speak
selected.reason: The Báb’s statement that what was revealed to Muhammad over twenty-three years God could have revealed in two days and nights, offered as a proof; a distinctive argument from the power of revelation.

selected.text: Yet in spite of all difficulties, he was ever in an exalted state; his face shone continually. He had the presence of a king. One cannot imagine such majesty. selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that in all difficulties Bahá’u’lláh had the presence of a king and drew strength from divine power; a vivid recollection of majesty in captivity.

selected.text: He hath quickened mankind with the spirit of guidance and hath rendered clear the White Path of Gifts, through the arguments which are brilliant and clear to the hearts of the intelligent, and whereby these hearts are moved, enlightened, illuminated and become cognizant of the Mighty Message in this Manifest Day of the Manifestation of the Honorable Station when the mystery of existence flows just as do the souls in the bodies.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on mankind quickened with the spirit of guidance through arguments clear to the hearts of the intelligent; links spiritual power with understanding.

selected.text: While in prison He withstood two despotic kings, and He gained victory over both. In prison He raised His Banner, He spread His Teachings and spiritually defeated two despotic kings. Such dominion appeared from Him, and such potency manifested from His personality.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that while in prison Bahá’u’lláh withstood and spiritually defeated two despotic kings; a narrative example addressed to youth.

The Blessed Perfection was imprisoned, yet he had that power to refuse anything or to do anything he wished
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá about the governor of ‘Akka refused admission for five years; a concrete narrative of the imprisoned One’s freedom.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s address describing a luminary, sea and spring whose effects renewed beings and raised the dead by its fragrances; a full image of renewal flowing from one centre.

selected.text: In Europe, in the great assemblies talks were given. I spoke to the eminent people. I remember that one day I met one of the members of Parliament. He asked me, 'What is the proof of his holiness Baha'u'llah-- I want it in a concise and useful form.' I said the concise and sufficient proof is that Baha'u'llah in such a prison as Acca, and when under chains, raised His banner. In Teheran He was in prison and under chains. In Acca he was in prison. Under these circumstances he raised it.' When I mentioned this proof he became very silent. I said, 'Just one word more. There is nothing recorded comparable to this. What power is this that from the beginning of the world until today such a thing has not happened
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá giving a member of Parliament the concise proof that Bahá’u’lláh raised His banner in prison and chains; a memorable narrative encounter.

selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that under the Blessed Beauty’s shadow the mosquito becomes a falcon and the atom a sun; opens the closing section on receiving power.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the trumpet blown, the graves risen and the world adorned with knowledge through His Pen; joins resurrection imagery with knowledge.

selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that persecutions increased the early believers’ power so that they lived in Heaven while on earth; a narrative of power received through steadfastness.

selected.reason: The Báb’s address in which all circle round the divine Will and worship God through the Countenance; a devotional close in the Báb’s voice.

selected.text: And moreover, the Bearer of this Most Great Tidings, this Ancient Light, this Straight Path, is possessed of a lofty and impregnable lineage and an exalted and surpassing honor. selected.reason: The Báb’s image of God preserving fire within a point of snow, with the warning that no deed is accepted without love for God’s loved one; joins a memorable image with a moral condition.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s glad tidings of Him Who was concealed behind the veil of grandeur and appeared with encompassing sovereignty; a full statement of hidden and revealed power.

selected.text: the Kingdom is the edification of the souls of men, the progress of the world of humanity, the manifestation of the love of God, the establishment of fellowship and unity amongst all peoples, the appearance of divine perfections, and the realization of the glory of the human race. This is the purpose of the advent of the Kingdom, and this is its result. Observe, then, how the edifying power of Baha'u'llah hath enlightened the darksome East, transformed voracious beasts into heavenly angels, endowed the ignorant with knowledge, and caused ravening wolves to become as gazelles in the meads of oneness. Those who used to burn the Holy Bible out of exceeding ignorance now set forth the truths and mysteries of the Old and New Testaments. In a brief span of time, He so educated His followers that, even in chains and stocks, and under the threat of swords and blades, they would raise the cry of "Ya Baha'u'l-Abha!" and would offer sugar candy to their executioners that they might strike the final blow with sweetened mouths

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on the Most Great Name arising under chains and sword to conquer East and West, with a heavenly palace in prison; a full argument from unparalleled power.

selected.text: Even as the visible sun that assisteth, as decreed by God, the true One, the Adored, in the development of all earthly things, such as the trees, the fruits, and colors thereof, the minerals of the earth, and all that may be witnessed in the world of creation, so do the divine Luminaries, by their loving care and educative influence, cause the trees of divine unity, the fruits of His oneness, the leaves of detachment, the blossoms of knowledge and certitude, and the myrtles of wisdom and utterance, to exist and be made manifest. Thus it is that through the rise of these Luminaries of God the world is made new, the waters of everlasting life stream forth, the billows of loving-kindness surge, the clouds of grace are gathered, and the breeze of bounty bloweth upon all created things. It is the warmth that these Luminaries of God generate, and the undying fires they kindle, which cause the light of the love of God to burn fiercely in the heart of humanity. It is through the abundant grace of these Symbols of Detachment that the Spirit of life everlasting is breathed into the bodies of the dead.

selected.text: Then look at the world of souls and spirits and hearts, that you may see how souls are inspired by their remembrance, at peace with their thought, content with their decree, well-pleased with their devotion, sanctified by their radiance, gladdened by their bestowal, illumined by their lights, receiving grace from the brilliance of their rays. And spirits are stirred by the breezes of their gardens, delighting in the bounties of their realities, rejoicing in the freshness of their meadows, gladdened by the fragrance of their thickets, made happy by the outpouring from their fountains. Hearts throb with love for them, tongues speak their praise. Consciousness is filled with spirit and fragrance by their sweet scents, and stays wakeful through nights and days by their gentle breezes. Beings receive grace from their outpourings, realities are purified by their manifestations, essences derive lights from their kindled fire, identities acquire mysteries from their abundant effusions.
